content.paragraph: In this section, we study two more rules of differentiation: the Product Rule and the Quotient Rule.

subsection.title: The Product Rule
subsection.paragraph: The derivative of the product of two differentiable functions is given by the following rule:
The derivative of the product of two functions is the first function times the derivative of the second plus the second function times the derivative of the first.
The Product Rule may be extended to the case involving the product of any finite number of functions (see Exercise 73). We prove the Product Rule at the end of this section.

note.title: Applied Example 7. Oxygen-Restoration Rate in a Pond
note.paragraph: When organic waste is dumped into a pond, the oxidation process that takes place reduces the pond’s oxygen content. How fast is the pond’s oxygen content changing $$1$$ day, $$10$$ days, and $$20$$ days after the organic waste has been dumped?
The rate of change of the pond’s oxygen level at any time $$t$$ is given by the derivative of the function $$f$$ . Thus, the required expression is

subsection.title: Verification of the Product Rule
subsection.paragraph: We will now verify the Product Rule. If $$p(x) = f(x)g(x)$$ , then
By adding $$- f(x + h)g(x) + f(x + h)g(x)$$ (which is zero!) to the numerator and factoring, we have

paragraph.math: $$\begin{array}{l} {p^{\prime}(x) = \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}\frac{f(x + h)\left\lbrack g(x + h) - g(x) \right\rbrack + g(x)\left\lbrack f(x + h) - f(x) \right\rbrack}{h}} \\ {\phantom{p^{\prime}(x)} = \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}\left\{ {f(x + h)\left\lbrack \frac{g(x + h) - g(x)}{h} \right\rbrack + g(x)\left\lbrack \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h} \right\rbrack} \right\}} \\ {\phantom{p^{\prime}(x)} = \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}f(x + h)\left\lbrack \frac{g(x + h) - g(x)}{h} \right\rbrack + \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}g(x)\left\lbrack \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h} \right\rbrack\qquad{\text{By Property}3\text{of limits}}} \\ {\phantom{p^{\prime}(x)} = \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}f(x + h) \cdot \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}\frac{g(x + h) - g(x)}{h} + \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}g(x) \cdot \lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}\frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}\qquad{\text{By Property}4\text{of limits}}} \\ {\phantom{p^{\prime}(x)} = f(x)g^{\prime}(x) + g(x)f^{\prime}(x)} \end{array}$$

subsection.paragraph: Observe that in the last link in the chain of equalities, we have used the fact that $$\lim\limits_{h\rightarrow 0}f(x + h) = f(x)$$ because $$f$$ is continuous at $$x$$ .

statement.paragraph: Find the derivative of $$f(x) = \frac{2x + 1}{x^{2} - 1}$$ .

answer.paragraph: We use the Quotient Rule to obtain

paragraph.math: $$\begin{array}{l} {f^{\prime}(x) = \frac{(x^{2} - 1)\frac{d}{\mathit{dx}}(2x + 1) - (2x + 1)\frac{d}{\mathit{dx}}(x^{2} - 1)}{\left( x^{2} - 1 \right)^{2}}} \\ {\phantom{f^{\prime}(x)} = \frac{\left( x^{2} - 1 \right)(2) - (2x + 1)(2x)}{\left( x^{2} - 1 \right)^{2}}} \\ {\phantom{f^{\prime}(x)} = \frac{2x^{2} - 2 - 4x^{2} - 2x}{\left( x^{2} - 1 \right)^{2}}} \\ {\phantom{f^{\prime}(x)} = \frac{- 2x^{2} - 2x - 2}{\left( x^{2} - 1 \right)^{2}}} \\ {\phantom{f^{\prime}(x)} = \frac{- 2\left( x^{2} + x + 1 \right)}{\left( x^{2} - 1 \right)^{2}}} \end{array}$$
